(St. Louis, Missouri) | college = [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]] (2019–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | career_start = 2023 | years1 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]]–[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team1 = [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] | years2 = {{nbay|2024|end}} | team2 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years3 = 2025 | team3 = [[Scarborough Shooting Stars]] | years4 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]] | team4 = [[Long Island Nets]] | years5 = 2025–2026 | team5 = [[Ironi Ness Ziona B.C.|Ironi Ness Ziona]] | years6 = [[2026–27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team6 = [[Memphis Hustle]] | highlights = * 2× [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball season assists leaders|NCAA assists leader]] (2022, 2023) * 2× First-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] (2022, 2023) * Atlantic 10 All-Defensive Team (2022) }} '''Yuri Collins''' (born March 7, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis Billikens]] of the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] (A-10), and has played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) as a member of the [[Golden State Warriors]]. ==High school career== Collins attended [[St. Mary's High School (St. Louis)|St. Mary's High School]]. As a senior, he averaged 22.6 points, 5.4 rebounds and 7.6 assists per game. Collins led St. Mary's to the Class 4 state championship game, averaging over 30 points per game during the team's postseason run.{{cite news |last1=Austin |first1=Earl |title=St. Louis American Boys "Fab Five" All-Star Basketball Team |url=https://www.stlamerican.com/sports/sports_columnists/inside_sports/st-louis-american-boys-fab-five-all-star-basketball-team/article_8115c6ac-5bf5-11e9-be9e-bf319c243137.html |access-date=August 2, 2022 |work=[[St. Louis American]] |date=April 11, 2019}} He committed to play college basketball at [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]] over offers from [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]], [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]], [[Missouri State Bears men's basketball|Missouri State]] and [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]]. ==College career== As a freshman, he averaged 5.4 points and 5.5 assists per game, leading all freshmen in assists.{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball Prepares for Pac-12 Tournament |url=https://uclabruins.com/news/2020/3/9/mens-basketball-mens-baskeball-prepares-for-pac-12-tournament.aspx |website=[[UCLA Bruins]] |access-date=August 2, 2022 |date=March 9, 2020}} Collins averaged 5.1 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 6.1 assists per game as a sophomore.{{cite web |title=ATLANTIC 10 ANNOUNCES 2021-22 PRESEASON MEDIA AND COACHES POLL |url=https://goexplorers.com/news/2021/10/27/mens-basketball-atlantic-10-announces-2021-22-preseason-media-and-coaches-poll.aspx |website=[[La Salle Explorers]] |access-date=August 2, 2022 |date=October 27, 2021}} He took on a leadership role for the Billikens as a junior due to an ACL tear suffered by [[Javonte Perkins]].{{cite news |last1=Durando |first1=Stu |title=SLU's Yuri Collins will leave after leading country in assists |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/college/slu/slus-yuri-collins-will-leave-after-leading-country-in-assists/article_27273f69-5cf3-5ea7-aafd-e5b3e56c213c.html |access-date=August 2, 2022 |work=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |date=April 18, 2022}} Collins was named to the First Team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] as well as the All-Defensive Team.{{cite news |last1=Durando |first1=Stu |title=Collins makes A-10 first team, all-defensive; Jimerson is third team |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/college/slu/billiken-beat/collins-makes-a-10-first-team-all-defensive-jimerson-is-third-team/article_2bb8583e-f565-5559-85d2-ddc1ac79daaf.html |access-date=August 2, 2022 |work=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |date=March 8, 2022}} He averaged 11.1 points, 4.1 rebounds and 7.9 assists per game, leading NCAA Division I in assists. Following the season, he entered the [[2022 NBA draft]] and the transfer portal.{{cite news |last1=Marsdale |first1=Sam |title=Saint Louis guard Yuri Collins announces entry into NCAA transfer portal |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Saint-Louis-guard-Yuri-Collins-announces-entry-into-NCAA-transfer-portal-186395654/ |access-date=August 2, 2022 |work=247 Sports |date=April 18, 2022}} Collins ultimately withdrew from the draft and returned to Saint Louis.{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Corey |title='Run it back': Yuri Collins will return to SLU for 2022-23 season with Billikens |url=https://www.ksdk.com/article/sports/college/slu/slu-point-guard-yuri-collins-returns/63-244b5ce3-5937-4aa5-8690-9352cad281e9 |access-date=August 2, 2022 |work=KSDK |date=April 25, 2022}} On November 30, 2022, he recorded 20 assists in a win over [[Tennessee State Tigers basketball|Tennessee State]], setting a school record and tying for the [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball players with 20 or more assists in a game|fourth-most in a single game]] in Division I history.{{Cite web |title=Collins has school-record 20 assists in Saint Louis' win |website=ABCnews.com |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/collins-school-record-20-assists-saint-louis-win-94257409 |access-date=December 1, 2022 |date=November 30, 2022 |archive-date=December 2, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221202024933/https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/collins-school-record-20-assists-saint-louis-win-94257409 |url-status=live }} ==Professional career== ===Santa Cruz / Golden State Warriors (2023–2025)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Collins joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|title=Collins Named to Golden State’s Summer League Roster|url=https://slubillikens.com/news/2023/6/29/mens-basketball-collins-named-to-golden-states-summer-league-roster.aspx|work=Saint Louis University|date=June 29, 2023|access-date=July 15, 2023}} and on October 16, he signed with them.{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Yuri Collins & Javonte Green to Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/yuri-collins-javonte-green-signed-20231016|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2023|access-date=October 16, 2023}} However, he was waived two days later{{cite web|title=Warriors Waive Guard Yuri Collins|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-waive-guard-yuri-collins-20231018|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2023|access-date=October 19, 2023}} and on October 30, he joined the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]].{{cite web|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Announce 2023 Training Camp Roster|url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2023-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 8, 2023}} After joining them for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]],{{cite web|title=Warriors Announce 2024 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-announce-2024-summer-league-roster-20240630|website=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2024|access-date=September 17, 2024}} Collins signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]] on September 13, 2024.{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Yuri Collins Returning To Warriors On Training Camp Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/yuri-collins-returning-to-warriors-on-training-camp-contract.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 14, 2024|access-date=September 17, 2024}} However, he was waived seven days later{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Warriors Waive Yuri Collins, Javan Johnson|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/warriors-waive-yuri-collins-javan-johnson.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 20, 2024|access-date=September 20, 2024}} and on October 28, he rejoined Santa Cruz.{{cite web|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Announce 2024 Training Camp Roster|url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2024-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 1, 2024}} On February 19, 2025, the [[Golden State Warriors]] signed Collins to a 10-day contract.{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Yuri Collins and Kevin Knox II to 10-Day Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-yuri-collins-and-kevin-knox-ii-to-10-day-contracts-20250219|website=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2025|access-date=February 20, 2025}} On February 23, Collins made his [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] debut against the [[2024–25 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]], scoring his first 2 career points in a 126-102 blowout victory. === Scarborough Shooting Stars (2025) === On May 17, 2025, Collins signed with the [[Scarborough Shooting Stars]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]] (CEBL).{{Cite web |date=May 17, 2025 |title=NBA Experienced Guard Collins Signs with Scarborough |url=https://www.cebl.ca/nba-experienced-guard-collins-signs-with-scarborough |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=www.cebl.ca |language=en}} === Long Island Nets (2025) === On September 9, 2025, Collin's returning player rights were traded to the [[Long Island Nets]] from the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] in exchange for a 2026 first-round pick and a 2026 second-round pick.{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2025 |title=Santa Cruz Warriors Trade Yuri Collins to the Long Island Nets |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DOZeXIhkeGO/?igsh=czV2ZXFkd3plaXJx}} On September 20, 2025, Collins signed a [[NBA salary cap|training camp deal]] with the [[Brooklyn Nets]], but was waived the next day.{{Cite web |last=Phillips-Keaton |first=Sharif |last2=read |first2=Nets Wire·2 min |date=September 21, 2025 |title=Nets waive G Yuri Collins ahead of NBA training camp |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/nets-waive-g-yuri-collins-230927922.html |access-date=November 20, 2025 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} He later signed with Long Island on November 3, 2025.{{Cite web |title=LONG ISLAND NETS ANNOUNCE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER |url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-announce-training-camp-roster-6 |access-date=November 20, 2025 |website=Long Island Nets |language=en}} === Ironi Ness Ziona (2025–2026) === On December 31, 2025, Collins signed with [[Ironi Ness Ziona B.C.|Ironi Ness Ziona]] of the Israeli [[Israeli Premier League|Ligat HaAl]].{{Cite web |title=ברוך הבא יורי קולינס! |url=https://ironinz.com/news.asp?id=70116 |access-date=2026-09-04 |website=עירוני "חי מוטורס" נס ציונה - הבית הכתום שלכם!}} === Memphis Hustle (2026–present) === On September 1, 2026, Collins was traded from the [[Long Island Nets]] to the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]] in a three team trade involving the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]].{{Cite web |title=Hustle Acquire Returning Player Rights to Yuri Collins From Nets |url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/hustle-acquire-returning-player-rights-to-yuri-collins-from-nets
